title: Westland Lynx - Wikipedia
abstract: The Westland Lynx is a British multi-purpose twin-engined military helicopter designed by Westland Helicopters, which was later taken over by AgustaWestland. It served in various roles such as battlefield utility, anti-armour, search and rescue, and anti-submarine warfare.
capability: Multi-purpose military helicopter with the ability to perform loops and rolls. Set the current Fédération Aéronautique Internationale's official airspeed record for helicopters in 1986.
rest_information: The Lynx was originally intended for civil and naval usage but was later adopted by the British Army, Royal Navy, German Navy, among others. It broke the world speed record over 15 and 25 km in 1986 with a speed of 400.87 km/h.

title: LYNX Helicopter XZ666 'Damien' | Ulster Aviation Society
capability: multi-role, military helicopter; capable of loops and rolls due to aerobatic capabilities; used in roles such as transport, armed escort, anti-tank warfare, reconnaissance, and evacuation missions
rest_information: Assembled in September 1978, XZ666 (nicknamed 'Damien') was modified with weapons hard points, uprated engines, and larger composite tail rotor. It served primarily as a utility helicopter by the 655 Squadron Army Air Corps from 1986-1990. Notable for its role during Operation Banner in Northern Ireland. Later used in NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) operations. Written off in 1994 and became a ground-instructional airframe before being received by the Ulster Aviation Society in February 2024.
